# Michael Wilt — Analytics Engineer

> Michael Wilt runs one-week teardowns of dbt projects: a model-by-model review
> that surfaces what the warehouse actually costs, where testing stops, and what
> is going to break next. Solo, fixed price, under his own name.

## Positioning

Analytics engineer helping teams fix slow, expensive, and fragile dbt projects —
and get their data AI-ready. Stack: dbt, Dagster, DLT, Python, Streamlit.

## The offer ladder

- The Look — free, 20 minutes. A live look at your dbt project; two or three real
  problems named out loud. No deliverable.
- The dbt Teardown — $2,500 intro, one week. Model-by-model review.
- The Fix Sprint — $3,000–$6,000, two weeks. Implementation of the top findings.
- Ongoing — $2,000–$4,000/month. A fixed block of hours, offered after a Fix Sprint.

Fixed price, never hourly. 50% up front. Two active engagements maximum.

## What the teardown covers

1. Structure and layering — staging/intermediate/marts discipline, DAG shape, fan-out.
2. Performance and cost — expensive models, materialization strategy, incremental logic.
3. Testing and data quality — coverage gaps and where trust breaks.
4. CI/CD and deployment — how changes ship and what is unguarded.
5. Documentation and lineage — what is undocumented or untraceable.
6. Naming and maintainability — conventions and drift.

Deliverables: a prioritized fix list naming specific models and files, a 20–30
minute recorded walkthrough, and a 30-day remediation roadmap.

## Best fit

- 15–200 employees
- dbt in production for 12+ months
- A 1–4 person data team with no dedicated analytics engineer
- Someone already complaining about warehouse costs or dashboard trust
